question: How did transformer model families, prompting paradigms, and full or parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies fit together as of late 2023?

key_findings.claim: The paper is a broad narrative catalog rather than a systematic review.
key_findings.evidence: It covers transformers, many text/vision/science model families, in-context and chain-of-thought prompting, agents, and adaptation methods, but gives no database search, inclusion criteria, quality appraisal, or structured evidence synthesis.

key_findings.claim: Its fine-tuning taxonomy spans task/domain adaptation, distillation, multitask learning, adapters, LoRA, prompt methods, and purported dynamic fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: The survey distinguishes updating all weights from freezing the backbone and training small modules or low-rank factors, then relates these choices to data and compute constraints.

key_findings.claim: The paper's own small classification study favors LoRA over full BERT fine-tuning but does not establish a general ordering.
key_findings.evidence: Table II reports mean F1 33.2 for BERT-base full tuning versus 82.2 for BERT-base LoRA and 86.8 for FLAN-T5-XL LoRA across six tasks, without repeated seeds, confidence intervals, matched optimization budgets, or a diagnosis of the anomalously weak full-tuning run.

key_findings.claim: The experimental conclusions are limited to a narrow convenience setup.
key_findings.evidence: BERT uses 32-bit and FLAN-T5 16-bit precision on an M2 accelerator; proposed future work includes ablations, other tasks, larger models, more PEFT methods, quantization comparisons, and loss analyses that would be needed to support broad claims.

key_findings.claim: Several descriptions blur adaptation categories and contain time-sensitive or weakly sourced product assertions.
key_findings.evidence: The document treats in-context prompting, retrieval, agents, full tuning, and PEFT in one landscape and frequently relies on project pages or secondary URLs; consequently it should be used as a historical map, not an authoritative benchmark.

method.core_idea: Organize a rapidly expanding set of LLM architectures, applications, prompting modes, and adaptation techniques in one tutorial document.
method.mechanism: Narratively summarize cited papers and projects, illustrate model families, then run a small six-task comparison of full tuning and LoRA across BERT and FLAN-T5 sizes.
assumptions: Breadth is more useful than systematic evidence grading
Reported source claims remain comparable across model families
A small local classification experiment illustrates general fine-tuning behavior

techniques.role: Groups heterogeneous model and adaptation developments into a tutorial sequence.
Contrasts updating all weights with low-rank trainable adapters on six classification tasks.

evaluations.setting: BERT-base/large and FLAN-T5 base/large/XL on six text-classification datasets
evaluations.metric: per-task and mean F1 plus trainable-parameter fraction
evaluations.result: reported mean F1 ranges from 33.2 for BERT-base full tuning to 86.8 for FLAN-T5-XL LoRA
evaluations.baseline: full BERT/FLAN-T5 tuning and LoRA variants; budgets are not shown to be matched

limitations: No systematic-review protocol or coverage audit.
No controlled seed variance or hyperparameter parity in the included experiment.
Coverage is frozen around December 2023 despite a 2024 arXiv identifier.
Some sources are secondary webpages and many commercial-model details are unverifiable.
failure_modes: Readers interpret taxonomy adjacency as empirical equivalence.
An under-tuned full baseline exaggerates PEFT gains.
Breadth obscures distinctions among prompting, retrieval, supervised tuning, and RL alignment.
reusable_insights: Separate adaptation by what changes at training time: data, prompts, added modules, or base weights.
Attach evidence level and date to every fast-moving model claim.
Benchmark PEFT with matched optimization and memory accounting.
open_questions: How would conclusions change under a reproducible systematic search?
Which PEFT method is Pareto-optimal for quality, memory, latency, and multi-task storage?
Why did the full BERT baseline fail so severely?

competitive_landscape.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Methods for Pretrained Language Models: A Critical Review and Assessment
competitive_landscape.difference: Xu et al. focus systematically on PEFT and include representative efficiency experiments; the reviewed paper ranges much more broadly across architectures, applications, prompting, and agents.

competitive_landscape.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Models: A Comprehensive Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Han et al. analyze PEFT algorithms together with system implementation costs; the reviewed paper offers a general LLM panorama with a much smaller adaptation experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Harnessing the Power of LLMs in Practice: A Survey on ChatGPT and Beyond
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. organize practical deployment, adaptation, and trustworthiness concerns; the reviewed paper devotes more space to enumerating model families and applications and less to deployment evidence.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The article is a comprehensive review of LLM paradigms and fine-tuning strategies with supporting experiments.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It assembles a large illustrated bibliography and one six-task LoRA/full-tuning table.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Its value is historical breadth and tutorial aggregation. Focused contemporary PEFT surveys are more systematic, and the uncontrolled experiment should not be treated as comparative evidence.

reviewer_notes: Read all 45 extracted pages with a second pass over taxonomy, experiment, challenges, conclusion, and references. Primary arXiv records for three competing surveys were checked on 2026-08-23.
